PullRequest.Title: Git - split the Repository from its SourceControl
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

The Git extension creates a `SourceControl` for every `Repository` it opens, so every repository it knows about also exists in core. This PR splits the two, so that a later change can keep a `Repository` without its `SourceControl` and create the `SourceControl` on demand. For example, a repository could be kept as a cache that skips repository discovery. Nothing detaches a repository yet, so behavior does not change.

## Commits

Each commit builds and passes the git tests on its own. The fourth commit addresses the review of the third.

1. **Keep resource state in Repository-owned groups.** The status model lived in the `SourceControl` resource groups, so it could not outlive the `SourceControl`. The four groups are now plain objects that `Repository` owns, and `Repository` copies each changed group into its source control. The commit template moves to `Repository` too.
2. **Extract `GitSourceControl`.** Every `vscode.scm` object of a repository, and the code that writes to it, moves into the new `extensions/git/src/sourceControl.ts`. That covers the source control and its groups, the input box settings, the count badge, the quick diff and artifact providers, the status bar commands, the action button and the SCM progress. `Repository` still creates it in its constructor.
3. **Attach and detach a repository's source control.** `Repository.attachSourceControl()` creates the `GitSourceControl` and starts the file watchers, auto fetch and configuration listeners. `detachSourceControl()` disposes them and keeps the `Repository`. `Model` attaches a repository's source control when it opens the repository. `Model.detachRepository()` has no caller yet.
4. **Fix reopening a detached repository.** Reopening reads the git directory again, and reuses a detached repository only while it is the same. A model update publishes only into the attachment that started it. `whenFirstStatus` restarts with each attachment.

## A detached repository

No code path reaches this yet. A detached repository:

- has no source control in core, no file watchers, no auto fetch and no model refresh on configuration changes. The history provider, branch protection provider and post-commit commands keep their configuration listeners, which only recompute settings in memory
- rejects git operations with "Repository is detached", and drops a model update that was running when it detached, even if it attaches again before git finishes
- is left out of `Model.repositories`, `Model.getRepository` and the git API. Detach fires `onDidCloseRepository` before it disposes the source control
- detaches its child repositories (worktrees and submodules) with it
- is reused when the repository opens again, as long as its git directory and root real path have not changed. Otherwise a new repository replaces it, so the trust request and the file watchers use the current git directory

## Compatibility

- The git extension API does not change. `git.d.ts` has no diff. The `ApiRepository` constructor throws for a repository without a source control, so the API cannot expose a detached one.
- Closing a repository works as before. Its children close while it is still open, and it keeps its disposed source control, so an extension that still holds it can run git operations and read its input box.
- Internally, `Repository.sourceControl`, `inputBox` and `artifactProvider` are now optional. Their callers in `commands.ts` and `diagnostics.ts` handle `undefined`, and `worktreeArtifacts.test.ts` asserts the provider exists.
- One difference is observable. At extension shutdown, a child repository fires `onDidCloseRepository` once instead of twice, because closing a repository twice is now a no-op.

## How to test

- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite git`: passed at the tip in 3 of 3 runs, with 134 passing, 4 pending and 0 failing (macOS). The first three commits pass on their own, with 129, 129 and 133 passing. The five new smoke tests cover detaching and reattaching a repository, reopening a detached repository whose git directory moved, detaching a parent with a worktree, a held repository after close, and a held worktree after its parent closes.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p extensions/git/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed at each commit.
- The tests for the fourth commit fail without it: the reattached repository's first status resolved before its groups were filled, and the reopened repository kept the old git directory.
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed.
- Source Control UI against base: a script ran Code OSS with the base git extension and with this branch. It used three fixture repositories: one with every kind of change, one with a merge conflict, and one with a submodule and a worktree. It captured the Source Control view, the input box, the action button, the activity bar badge, the status bar and the Explorer decorations through Stage All, commit, and closing the parent repository. All 11 captured states were identical. This ran before the rebase onto the latest `main`.
- To try it by hand, open a folder with a repository that has staged, unstaged, untracked and conflicting changes, plus a submodule. The Source Control view, the status bar, staging, committing and closing repositories should behave as on `main`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover and open repositories at extension startup or when an editor exposes a new repository
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository-root and git-directory discovery, realpath resolution, trust request, Source Control creation, and watcher setup precede publishing the opened repository. Initial status is queued without awaiting it, so Git metadata/status does not block repository publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run rev-parse for root discovery and git-directory discovery, with additional root normalization calls only for applicable path cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally two Git subprocesses per newly opened distinct root, not per changed file; existing exact repositories skip discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same root and git-directory discovery calls were awaited before creating Repository.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read git config and resolve realpath; establish a recursive working-tree watcher, two git-directory/worktrees watchers, and an upstream watcher when applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One config read and one realpath resolution per new opening; three baseline watchers per attached repository, plus a conditional upstream watcher.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same reads and watchers existed; watcher setup moved from Repository construction into attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery and initial watcher establishment precede publication; later upstream watcher refresh follows status.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request resource trust and register/configure Source Control and its four resource groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trust request and one Source Control per distinct attached root; four resource groups are registered together by the existing 100ms debounce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent trust and SCM operations occurred in the same opening workflow, with SCM ownership inside Repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Trust is awaited; Source Control registration is issued before opened-repository publication; resource-group registration is deferred/coalesced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct repository roots after existing-repository checks; child discovery remains capped by configured submodule/worktree detection limits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model.openRepository is sequentialized on the Model instance. Initial status has a shared limiter of five repositories; each status itself performs parallel metadata reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Already-open exact repositories return early. Detached reuse requires matching root, git directories, bare status, and realpath, but still performs discovery/trust checks. No production caller currently populates the detached cache. Resource-state publication tracks array identity; count/template setters also suppress unchanged IPC.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete opening diff, sequentialize decorator, initial-status limiter, watcher implementations, and SCM batching were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository counts and filesystem/process latency vary; no durations were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Extraction retains discovery call counts, watcher cardinality, initial-status concurrency, and the non-awaited status scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh status after file changes, staging, committing, or relevant configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Write operations await the same model refresh: parallel metadata/template reads finish before parallel status and refs reads, then resource groups and status notifications are published. Filesystem-triggered refresh is deferred until idle/focused.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve branch/upstream, obtain commit template, run git status and for-each-ref, with conditional rebase-commit and cold virtual-filesystem config queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One status and one refs subprocess per completed refresh, plus a template query when merge/squash messages are absent and branch/upstream-dependent queries; no new per-resource subprocesses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same two-phase refresh and conditional subprocess calls were present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by status/write-operation completion; status/refs begin after metadata completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read HEAD, config, .gitmodules, merge/squash/rebase state, optional template contents, and worktree metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed set of reads/probes per refresh plus main HEAD/readdir and two sequential reads per linked worktree; unchanged fallback Git reads apply on existing failure paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical metadata reads and worktree enumeration were already required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata reads are on the refresh critical path; worktree reads remain sequential within their metadata task.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy changed resource arrays into SCM, sort/diff snapshots, serialize resource splices, and update count/template/context information.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most four changed groups per model publication. Array-identity tracking prevents the added template-publication update from resubmitting unchanged groups; SCM resource updates retain the existing 100ms coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Resource-group setters performed the same defensive copies and downstream snapshot/serialization work directly from Repository; reading groups also defensively copied arrays.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Array publication is synchronous in the extension host; snapshot/IPC work is deferred/coalesced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Changed resources up to the configured status limit (default 10000), refs, attached repository count, and registered worktrees; worktree enumeration performs two reads per linked worktree.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Metadata requests use Promise.all, followed by status/refs Promise.all. Initial statuses are globally limited to five. Runtime status is throttled per Repository with at most one current and one pending call; file events additionally use a 1000ms debounce and 5000ms post-refresh wait. Direct configuration refresh scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Virtual-filesystem configuration is initialized once per Repository, including a cached false result. Commit-template absence remains uncached and is queried during refresh as before. Repository-owned arrays remove defensive-copy getter costs; GitSourceControl copies only groups with new array identities. SCM count/template setters deduplicate equal values.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for scheduling, boundaries, and deduplication: refresh callers, status parser limit, SCM setters, and snapshot batching were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large working trees and refs can make existing refresh work expensive. The new pre-status update can recompute the tracked-count filter, but it does not add group serialization and replaces several prior getter copies; no high-confidence net degradation was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. No boundary fan-out was introduced, and unchanged resource groups are not republished by the extra update call.

Scenarios.Scenario: Periodic automatic fetch and SCM operation progress
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Automatic fetch waits for an idle/focused repository and runs in the background. Progress/input enablement responds to existing operation events rather than introducing a new awaited operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch default or all remotes through Git.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fetch operation per enabled repository per loop period, with Git remote fan-out for fetch-all unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repository construction created the same AutoFetcher, loop, fetch options, and throttling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the repository-opening critical path; awaited within each background loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update commit input enablement and invoke SCM progress for operation lifecycle events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing operation-event-driven updates; progress end remains debounced by 300ms.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same ProgressManager implementation lived in repository.ts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Progress observation does not add awaited Git work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Attached repositories with autofetch enabled and configured fetch period; remote count when fetch-all is selected.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fetch loop per enabled repository with per-method throttling; no new cross-repository limiter or burst is introduced. The idle wait yields before the attachment is assigned, preventing synchronous startup fetch execution during constructor setup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Enablement/configuration is maintained per AutoFetcher. Detach disposes the fetcher; normal attachment still creates one fetcher per repository. Authentication-failure disabling and periodic wake-up behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: AutoFetcher construction, idle wait, loop, throttle, and extracted ProgressManager were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency and enabled-repository counts are workload-dependent; no measurement was made.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Expensive fetch scheduling is preserved, and attachment disposal owns the existing background fetcher.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show quick diff for visible files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Original-resource lookup awaits filesystem stat and, for eligible tracked working-tree resources, check-ignore before returning the Git URI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat eligible file resources to exclude symbolic links.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per eligible provider request, potentially two when both providers request the same file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same providers and stat calls were configured directly by Repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the original-resource URI is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run check-ignore with eligible paths passed over stdin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process for each eligible working-tree original-resource request; staged provider does not add this process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical ignore checks and request cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before returning the working-tree original-resource URI.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible file/provider requests after scheme, repository, hidden-state, and group-membership checks; group membership scans depend on changed-file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent provider requests can run concurrently; the extraction adds no per-file scheduling or limiter changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new quick-diff result cache is introduced. Repository-owned groups avoid full-array defensive copies on membership reads; membership checks and ignore checks retain their prior behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both provider implementations and checkIgnore process creation were read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible-file request frequency and changed-group sizes vary; no quick-diff timings were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Passing the existing Repository into relocated provider setup does not increase filesystem/process calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse branches, tags, stashes, and worktree artifacts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Artifact requests await their existing Git/filesystem reads before sorting and returning artifact DTOs. Provider construction only creates groups/listeners and does not eagerly fetch artifacts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read refs or stashes; worktree detail requests query branch refs together and read detached commits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query for a branches, tags, or stashes group; nonempty worktree details use one grouped refs query plus D detached-commit calls, not one refs query per worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same GitArtifactProvider and getWorktreeDetails implementation with identical grouping/fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read main HEAD, enumerate worktree metadata folders, and read each linked worktree HEAD/gitdir.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One main HEAD read and directory enumeration plus two reads per linked worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical enumeration for worktree artifact requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Map requested artifacts into DTOs and convert commands for IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One DTO per returned artifact; existing command-disposable replacement is retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same artifact serialization path; extraction merely relocates provider assignment.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Requested artifact group, branch/tag/stash counts, worktree count W, and detached-worktree count D.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Worktree metadata filesystem reads are sequential per linked worktree; detached-worktree commit reads use Promise.all without a new limiter. Branch/tag/stash reads remain one logical query per requested group.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Worktree change notification compares a sorted path/ref key across statuses. Artifact requests retain existing uncached reads. Branch worktree commit details are grouped into one refs query; detached worktree commits are fetched separately as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor laziness, artifact methods, grouped refs queries, detached-commit fan-out, and downstream serialization were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing detached-worktree fan-out can be expensive for large D but is not changed by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The existing fan-out and serialization are not introduced or materially amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Detach/reopen a repository, or close a parent repository while extensions retain API objects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detach recursively removes children, publishes close events, and disposes SCM/watchers/fetchers. Reopen reruns discovery and attaches a new SCM before publication. Normal close still permits held API objects to perform operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose/unregister SCM groups/providers and release watcher registrations; reattach recreates SCM/watcher registrations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One attachment cleanup per repository in the affected child tree; closed guard prevents duplicate close cleanup/events. Reopen recreates the same attachment resources as a fresh open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normal close performed equivalent cleanup while discarding Repository. Detach/reuse did not exist; normal parent close could reenter a child's close path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup occurs during detach/close; creation precedes reopened-repository publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reopening performs existing discovery and queued status. Held normally closed API objects can still run requested Git operations; detached objects reject before spawning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing discovery/status calls per reopen and requested Git operations per retained API invocation; detach itself adds no Git process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reopening a closed root created a fresh Repository with the same discovery/status boundaries. Held closed API objects already could perform operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reopen discovery is awaited; initial status is not. Requested held-object operations retain their existing awaited behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Attached parent/child repository tree and, if detach becomes reachable, distinct detached roots retained for the Model lifetime. Current detachRepository callers are smoke tests only.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Detach/close cleanup is synchronous; reopening is Model-sequentialized and first status uses the shared five-repository limiter. In-flight model updates are canceled/dropped when their attachment changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Detached repositories are reused only for matching locations, disposed on location mismatch or Model disposal, and removed from the detached list when reopened. Reattachment clears model state and resets first-status. Normal close retains its disposed SCM as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for ownership, cancellation, reuse checks, and the absence of production detach callers: repository-wide caller search and smoke-test additions were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Detached-cache growth and repeated detach/attach overhead have no current production trigger. A future caller would need a separate lifecycle/cardinality review.
Scenarios.Verdict: No currently reachable retention/concurrency regression. Normal cleanup preserves its prior expensive boundaries, and duplicate close handling is bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 11 changed files and all diff pages. Traced repository discovery, status/write refresh, automatic fetch, SCM serialization, quick diff, artifact queries, and lifecycle cleanup; found no high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression. No changed/transitive database boundary was found. Review was static. An incidental reduction in defensive resource-array copies was identified, but the copy getter's introducing provenance could not be resolved, so no regression-fix learning signal was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
